{"id":"project-LICHEN-ow1e.157","title":"Schnorr signature s=0 rejection may be overly strict","description":"**Location:** python/src/lichen/crypto/schnorr48.py:138-140

**Risk:** The verify function rejects signatures where `s == 0` (line 139). While `s == 0` is mathematically valid only in degenerate cases, rejecting it without logging may cause confusion when debugging interop issues.

**Context:** The rejection of `s == 0` is correct for security (it indicates the nonce was zero, which should never happen with deterministic nonce derivation). However, `s >= L` rejection (line 139) catches non-canonical scalars.

**Maintainer burden:** If a buggy implementation sends non-canonical signatures, users will get silent verification failures with no hint about why.

**Suggestion:** Log at DEBUG level when rejecting for `s == 0` or `s >= L` to aid debugging.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"me@mark.atwood.name","created_at":"2026-07-06T15:38:29.735584Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-07-06T17:44:48.691565Z","closed_at":"2026-07-06T17:44:48.691565Z","close_reason":"Closed","labels":["maintainer-burden","owner-reserved","review","risk"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"project-LICHEN-ow1e.157","depends_on_id":"project-LICHEN-ow1e","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-07-06T15:38:29.73675Z"}]}
